items.sentence: The MHRA says it approved retifanlimab (Zynyz) on 6 July 2026 as the first treatment for adults with advanced Merkel cell skin cancer.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: The approval is for cancer that has spread or returned and cannot be cured with surgery or radiotherapy, and it came through the International Recognition Procedure.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: The MHRA explains that retifanlimab is an immunotherapy that helps the body's immune system recognise and attack cancer cells.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: It is given as a diluted intravenous infusion over 30 minutes.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: The MHRA reports that in a study of 101 adults who had not previously been treated for advanced disease, 53.5% responded to retifanlimab.
